items.title: Do not use pager for root `uv help` and improve after help hint
items.reason: Explicitly made bare `uv help` an unpaged, short-form overview. Its rationale describes the root help as a landing page; the current source retains the same exclusion. This directly explains the reported behavior.

items.title: Respect `PAGER` env var when paging in `uv help` command
items.reason: Added PAGER support. In its comments, another user reported the same difference with PAGER=less; a maintainer explained that bare `uv help` does not page, and the user confirmed `uv help run` does. Pager selection does not override the root-help exclusion.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs using literal terms 'uv help', 'pager', 'paging', and 'no paging'; conceptual terms included help with scroll, root, top-level, pagination, and area:cli/page. Also searched the reported version and closed pager/less fixes. PR keyword searches returned no hits, so issue references and help.rs commit history were followed to inspect historical PRs, comments, reviews, and patches. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#16914 and astral-sh/uv#16015 (BusyBox option failures), astral-sh/uv#16878 (missing colors), and astral-sh/uv#16913 (pager prompt text). No matching unresolved defect or regression was found.

type_reason: The reporter asks whether the difference is intentional. The explicit design rationale in astral-sh/uv#4936, the maintainer clarification in astral-sh/uv#5511, and the current `!is_root` paging condition establish intended behavior. No malfunction or regression is established, and the report does not explicitly request a behavior change. These historical PRs explain the design rather than track an outstanding problem or request to duplicate.
summary: astral-sh/uv#4936 intentionally disabled paging for bare `uv help`; astral-sh/uv#5511 contains a maintainer answer to the same question about PAGER=less.
draft_response: This is intentional: bare `uv help` prints the command overview without a pager, while `uv help <command>` pages the detailed help when stdout is a terminal. That distinction was introduced in astral-sh/uv#4936 and confirmed in the discussion on astral-sh/uv#5511. Your observation matches uv's behavior; `$PAGER=less` does not enable paging for the overview. To page it explicitly, use `uv help | less`.
